prerequisites: Must master the obtaining of effort laws for simple bar structures.

learning_outcomes.text: Apply the principles of materials resistance in the selection of materials used in engineering.
Recognize and understand the principles of materials resistance that apply to engineering.
Recognize and understand the training needs that will be useful to successfully solve new situations related to industrial engineering.
Propose creative solutions to satisfactorily respond to real needs and problems of society.
Develop professional texts and scientific-technical reports according to the conventions of the field of industrial technical engineering.
Adapt the organization of content and the use of language, verbal and non-verbal, to argue in various situations or before various audiences.
Develop measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other works typical of the field of technical engineering.
Apply the knowledge of industrial engineering in learning new methods and theories.
Critically and constructively show the advantages and opportunities of different solutions to the same problem.
Apply the fundamentals of elasticity and materials resistance to the behavior of real solids.
Recognize and understand the fundamentals of elasticity and materials resistance that apply to the behavior of real solids.

syllabus_topics: BLOCK I.- STUDY OF DEFORMATIONS AND MOVEMENTS. HYPERSTATIC STRUCTURES.
Deformations produced by axial force. Elongations-shortenings.
Hyperstatic bars subjected to axial force.
Mixed sections subjected to axial force.
Differential equation of the elastic line.
Elasticity and Strength of Materials: Elastic Solids.
Concept of stress. Stress tensor. Equilibrium at the boundary. Principal stresses and directions.
Concept of deformation: Strain tensor. Compatibility conditions for deformations.
Theme 5: WORK AND ENERGY IN ELASTIC SOLIDS
Deformation energy. Work of external forces.
Internal deformation energy in straight bars.
Calculation of reactions and movements using virtual work theorems.
BLOCK IV: INTRODUCTION TO THE FINITE ELEMENT METHOD
Theme 6: INTRODUCTION TO THE FINITE ELEMENT METHOD (FEM).
Introduction to the use of commercial software for structural analysis using FEM.
Deformations due to axial and bending forces.
